title: M60 lua LUA-15 — a member's identity is its container plus its own name, recorded once

checks.name: every method is a symbol under its OWN name with its owner
no symbol name contains '.' or ':' (a path, not a name)
no symbol name duplicates its own owner
each owner is itself a symbol
a plain function has no owner
a member is a method and a plain function is a function
every method call target joins to a declaration of that name
each member is filed at its own declaration line
a function nested in another function is scoped to it, not to global
the nested function is filed at its own declaration line
the contains edge for a nested function names its enclosing function
a top-level function is still scoped to global
a top-level closure's internal return is NOT published as a file export
a closure's own local is not attributed to an enclosing NAMED function
the unmutated symbols pass every expectation
the export leg is not vacuous: the fixture's real export IS published

detail.name: LUA-15 again: the name is the full qualified text

mutants.method: output mutation — the engine caches analyzer modules, so in-process source mutation has no effect

limitations: The call-to-declaration join test asserts that a symbol exists whose name IS the call target. It does not assert the RECEIVER matches, because the call edge does not carry one — under LUA-13 the receiver is dropped from the edge. Adding it is a separate change with its own trade-off (an unqualified target cannot be resolved, which is why `M.new` and `Account:new` are currently indistinguishable on the wire).
The fixture is one file with five declarations. It exercises each shape but is not a corpus; script/m60/lua-truth-oracle.ts is the corpus-scale check on the same contract.
